Ozeryany New Jewish Cemetery (Ternopil Region)

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopil Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. According to the Yizkor memorial book for Ozeryany, an ohel of R. Velvele, a descendant of the Baal Shem Tov, once stood at this cemetery. Ozeryany's Jewish community, present from at least the late 18th century, peaked at 1,558 people (48.1 percent of the town) in 1880, and was touched by both the Haskalah and Zionist movements by then. Hungarian forces occupied the town in July 1941, and the Gestapo arrived two months later to establish a ghetto; on September 26, 1942, 700 Jews were deported to the Bełżec death camp, and the remaining 500 were sent to other ghettos that October. This is the newer of Ozeryany's two Jewish cemeteries, presumed established in the second half of the 19th century after the Old cemetery, documented elsewhere in this collection, was closed.
